I have been working this land for 55 years. My wife and I only have 5 mu left — the children went to the city long ago. I do what I know works. Last year's harvest was fair, so I will do about the same this year.

My main land is wheat-maize — I plant wheat in October and then maize right after the wheat comes off in June. Four mu I keep for this rotation. The other one mu near the road I still plant cotton like I always did, even though cotton is a lot of work for us old people — but I know how to grow it.

For wheat, I buy two bags of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind, 50 jin each bag) per mu before plowing — that is what the shop sells and what everyone in the village uses. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I broadcast one bag of urea per mu with the irrigation water. I water three times: once before winter, once at green-up, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — once for aphids, once for rust if I see yellow spots. I use rotary tillage because the hire-man with the machine does it cheap, 40 yuan per mu.

For maize, I do not plow — I just drill the seed right into the wheat stubble, saves work and time. I buy hybrid seed from the same dealer every year, the "Zhengdan" kind my neighbor also plants. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then side-dress urea when the maize is knee-high. I water once or twice if the rain does not come. I spray for borer and armyworm.

For cotton, I plough deep in spring because cotton needs loose soil. I use improved seed. Cotton eats a lot of spray — bollworm, aphid, mite — I spray maybe seven or eight times through the summer. That is the cost of cotton. Yield is not what it was twenty years ago but the price is okay.

I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than lose yield. A bag costs 120 yuan, but losing 100 jin of grain costs more.
